tasks.short: Supervise clerical staff, coach individuals and arrange training.

steps.what: Review upcoming work and training records to identify coverage gaps.
Discuss difficulties, learning needs and development interests with clerical staff.
Assign routine work and approve training within delegated limits.
Adapt procedures and examples into training materials.

loop.input: Approved procedures, learning objectives and selected examples without unnecessary personal data.
loop.output: Training draft with exercises and references to source sections.
loop.check: Check source references, procedural accuracy and suitability for the learner before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved sections return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but adapting prose and examples to learning needs requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Find suitable times and send training invitations.
Demonstrate tasks, observe practice and give individual feedback.
Record attendance and verified course completion.
Review progress with staff and agree further support.

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} and {CALENDAR} to enrol staff, schedule agreed training and record verified completion. A small service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines training records with the {PROJECT} work plan to flag factual coverage gaps, while a bounded drafting loop prepares materials from approved procedures in the {DOCS}. The assistant approves materials and handles coaching, work allocation and individual support.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training records, work plans and procedures sit separately. Individual coaching needs cannot be reduced to course completion rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and calendar settings handle routine administration. AI coding reduces the effort of building connectors and templates; bounded drafting can adapt approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Completion does not prove competence. GDPR limits access and reuse of staff information; national rules may require consultation, and automated staff allocation or monitoring would need a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, build trust, demonstrate judgement and adapt feedback to the person.

ambition.what: Cross-cover training for part-time clerical staff

tasks.altitude: The week contains more coaching and practical cross-cover exercises. With manager delegation, the assistant could approve routine cross-training within an agreed budget; the software itself grants no decision rights.

reach.task: Plan clerical service coverage during absence.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, service priorities and the limits of delegated staffing authority.

reach.task: Coordinate training for a procedure rollout.
reach.learn: Dependencies, adoption measures and rollout planning.

evidence.claim: Enrolment rules, calendar configuration and record connectors are established implementation patterns; local savings are estimates.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can prepare an invitation and agenda from a mail thread; this supports scheduling preparation, not supervision.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation found scheduling took longer, supporting a configuration-first approach and local testing.
The EU AI Act includes AI literacy obligations and provisions concerning employment-related allocation and monitoring.

assumptions: The assistant has delegated responsibility for routine clerical work allocation and training coordination.
A typical setup uses the {LMS}, {PROJECT}, {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}; local arrangements vary.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Automatic enrolment and invitations stay within an approved training plan and spending limits.
Build ranges cover a small pilot using existing systems, not a replacement learning platform.
unknowns: Which systems hold training records, work plans and approved procedures?
Can the installed {LMS} configure enrolments, completion evidence and calendar connections?
Which training and work-allocation decisions are delegated to the assistant?
Which national consultation requirements and employee representative arrangements apply?
Are approved materials current, accessible and suitable for reuse?
What is the measured local time split?
research_questions: Does configuration cover enrolment and scheduling without a custom connector?
Can factual coverage gaps be shown without scoring individual performance?
Do adapted exercises improve observed task competence after review?
new_work: Review generated training materials and their source references.
Handle unavailable courses, scheduling conflicts and missing completion evidence.
Maintain course mappings, access permissions and connectors.
Refresh training examples when approved procedures change.

tasks.short: Review office procedures, reporting and spending to recommend practical improvements.

steps.what: Agree the process, problem and limits of the review.
Retrieve spending and workflow records for the agreed period.
Reconcile exports and calculate spending, volumes and turnaround times.
Ask staff how work actually flows and where delays arise.
Compare written procedures with observed practice and reporting requirements.

loop.input: Approved procedures, reporting requirements and staff-validated process observations.
loop.output: Draft differences table with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require references for each finding; the assistant verifies meaning, omissions and conflicting evidence.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedures and observations express equivalent or conflicting requirements in varied prose.

steps.what: Assess improvement options against cost, service quality and staff constraints.
Prepare a recommendation with costs, measures and a proposed trial.
Decide whether to approve a trial and assign responsibility.
Compare trial results with the baseline and report unresolved effects.

tasks.design: Scheduled, read-only connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieve scoped records from the {ERP} and {PROJECT}; deterministic checks produce a baseline and trial comparisons in the {BI}. A bounded loop compares procedures in the {DOCS} with validated observations, and a template generator assembles the assistant's selected recommendation. Staff discussions, trade-offs and change approval remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exports use different identifiers and definitions. Written procedures omit informal workarounds, so a report alone cannot explain delays or establish a good change.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small connectors, reconciliation checks and report templates cheaper to build. Bounded text comparison can prepare findings with references for review.
tasks.still_hard: Poor records limit causal claims, and lower spending can conceal extra work elsewhere. GDPR, access controls and national employee consultation rules apply; individual monitoring would require separate assessment under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish useful controls from avoidable friction and negotiate changes that staff can sustain.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on whether office workflow trials should continue

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to rebuilding evidence packs, leaving more time to test explanations with staff. With explicit delegation, the assistant could initiate small, reversible trials within agreed service and budget limits.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a process change improved service.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, comparison groups, confounding factors and whole-process costs.
Business cases, service commitments and budget authority.

evidence.claim: Scheduled exports, deterministic reconciliation, dashboards and template reports are established patterns; this digest provides no direct case for this exact task.
A bounded text comparison can prepare procedure findings, but its accuracy and time savings need local testing.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting savings but no evidence of higher productivity and observed hallucinations.
Employment-related monitoring or allocation can bring additional EU AI Act requirements; ordinary report preparation is a different use.

assumptions: The assistant prepares recommendations; an authorised manager approves operational changes.
Today, exports from the {ERP} and {PROJECT} are consolidated in the {SPREADSHEET}.
The baseline uses process-level measures rather than individual employee rankings.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one office process with accessible exports and a limited trial.
Consent and access ranges include consultation work where applicable; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Which records contain usable timestamps, costs and process identifiers?
Are metric definitions agreed across departments?
Can read-only exports or interfaces be authorised?
Which procedures are current and who approves their interpretation?
Which national consultation rules apply to the proposed data use?
Can the assistant initiate trials, and within which limits?
How much time is currently spent collecting evidence versus assessing changes?
research_questions: Can existing reports provide the baseline before building new connectors?
Do recorded timestamps represent actual work or delayed data entry?
Which service measure would reveal costs displaced to another team?
How often do reviewed text comparisons reveal useful, verified procedure differences?
new_work: Resolve unmatched records and maintain metric definitions.
Verify source references and challenge unsupported procedure findings.
Maintain connectors, report templates and access permissions.
Check whether trial outcomes reflect the change or other events.
Retire measures and reports that no longer inform decisions.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward coaching clerical staff and coordinating evidence-based office improvements. Wider authority depends on explicit delegation for training budgets and small operational trials.
reach: Administrative services management through service coverage and training planning.
Management analysis through baseline measures and evaluation of process trials.
Project coordination through procedure rollouts and adoption support.
skills_to_grow: Basic reconciliation and data quality review.
Checking generated text against approved sources.
Trial design and interpretation of results.
Access governance, GDPR and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: An office improvement coordinator who develops clerical capability, runs small approved workflow trials and brings managers verified evidence for service and spending decisions.

job.title: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
